info.name: Meetup
info.description:
End-to-end happy path for the Meetup modular-monolith sample (baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:5123).

AUTHENTICATION (Authentik, PKCE-only public client): every business endpoint requires a JWT from the Authentik `meetup` application — anonymous calls get 401, wrong-role calls get 403. There is no password login endpoint. Steps:

1. Create a PKCE pair (any generator): code_verifier (43-128 chars) + code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier)).
2. Open in a browser (fill in YOUR challenge/state):
   {{authentikUrl}}/application/o/authorize/?client_id=meetup&redirect_uri=http://localhost:5123/auth/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid profile email&state=xyz&code_challenge=<CHALLENGE>&code_challenge_method=S256
   Log in as a dev user (alice / bob / carol, see Auth folder). Authentik redirects to http://localhost:5123/auth/callback?code=<CODE> (the API has no such route — copy CODE from the address bar).
3. Exchange the code:
   POST {{authentikUrl}}/application/o/token/ (form-urlencoded): grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=meetup&code=<CODE>&redirect_uri=http://localhost:5123/auth/callback&code_verifier=<VERIFIER>
4. Paste the access_token into the collection variable authToken (all requests send it as Bearer automatically).

DEV USERS (passwords are local-dev only): alice / MeetupAlice123! (meetup-members), bob / MeetupBob123! (members+organizers), carol / MeetupCarol123! (members+organizers+admins).

ROLE MATRIX: member self-service (register, meetings view/join/comment, buy subscription, pay fee) is permission-only; proposing needs meetup-organizers; confirm/decide/admin listings need meetup-admins.

RUN ORDER on a fresh database: Health → Registrations (register as alice-token, confirm+list as carol-token) → UserAccess (carol) → Administration (propose as bob-token, accept/list as carol-token) → Payments → Meetings. Requests capture ids into collection variables (registrationId, proposalId, groupId, meetingId, subscriptionId, meetingFeePaymentId, commentId) so the flow chains automatically. Switch authToken when a folder needs a different role.

IMPORTANT: several endpoints bind the id from BOTH the route and the body — the body value MUST equal the route value or the handler throws (HTTP 500). The bodies below already reference the matching {{variable}}.

variable.description: Paste an Authentik access_token here (see collection description). Use alice/bob/carol tokens per the folder's required role.

item.name: Health
item.description: Anonymous (no token needed, though the collection sends one if set).

item.name: Auth
item.description: How to mint tokens (Authentik is PKCE-only — no client secret, no password grant). Dev users: alice / MeetupAlice123! (meetup-members), bob / MeetupBob123! (members + meetup-organizers), carol / MeetupCarol123! (members + organizers + meetup-admins). The token-exchange request below needs a CODE obtained via the browser authorize URL from the collection description (replace <CHALLENGE> state/code first, then replace <CODE> and <VERIFIER> here). On success copy response.access_token into the authToken collection variable.

item.name: Login - run 1: get link, run 2: exchange code

exec: // FIRST RUN: this prints your personal login link to the Postman Console
// (View > Show Postman Console). Open it in a browser, log in, copy the
// CODE from the address bar, paste it into the auth_code collection
// variable, then press Send on this request again to get your token.
for (var i = 0; i < 64; i++) { verifier += chars.charAt(Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length)); }
console.log('OPEN THIS LINK IN YOUR BROWSER TO LOG IN:' + String.fromCharCode(10) + link);

item.name: Registrations
item.description: 1. Register (member token, e.g. alice; a fresh login is generated per Send) → 2. Verify UserRegistered (admin token, e.g. carol: user exists, inactive) → 3. Confirm (admin) → 4. Verify UserRegistrationConfirmed (admin: user active) → 5. List (admin). The Verify steps prove each integration event crossed the module boundary (see docs/end-to-end-test-guide.md).

exec: // Each Send registers a fresh user so re-runs never clash with old rows.

item.name: Verify UserRegistered event → user created, inactive (admin)
item.description: Run with an ADMIN token (e.g. carol), ~10s after Register user — the outbox relay polls every ~5s, so re-send until green. Proves the cross-module effect of UserRegisteredIntegrationEvent: Registrations stored it in its transactional outbox, the relay delivered it, and UserAccess consumed it through its inbox (CreateUserOnRegistrationHandler), creating an inactive user.

exec: pm.test('status is 200 (log in as admin, e.g. carol)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
var user = pm.response.json().data.find(function (u) { return u.login === login; });
pm.test('UserRegistered event created user ' + login, function () { pm.expect(user).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test('new user is inactive until confirmed', function () { pm.expect(user && user.isActive).to.be.false; });

item.name: Verify UserRegistrationConfirmed event → user active (admin)
item.description: Run with an ADMIN token (e.g. carol), ~10s after Confirm — re-send until green. Proves UserRegistrationConfirmedIntegrationEvent travelled Registrations → UserAccess and ActivateUserOnConfirmationHandler flipped the user active.

exec: pm.test('status is 200 (log in as admin, e.g. carol)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
var user = pm.response.json().data.find(function (u) { return u.login === login; });
pm.test('confirmed user ' + login + ' is active', function () { pm.expect(user && user.isActive).to.be.true; });

item.name: UserAccess
item.description: Admin only (carol token). The user appears here after its registration is confirmed.

item.name: Administration
item.description: 1. Propose (organizer token, e.g. bob) → 2. Accept (admin token, e.g. carol) → 3. Verify ProposalAccepted (any member: the group exists in Meetings, groupId captured) → 4. List. Reject is the negative path (admin).

item.name: Verify ProposalAccepted event → group created
item.description: Any member token, ~10s after Accept proposal — re-send until green. Proves MeetingGroupProposalAcceptedIntegrationEvent travelled Administration → Meetings and CreateGroupOnProposalAcceptedHandler materialized the group (it also captures groupId for the Meetings folder).

exec: var group = pm.response.json().data.find(function (g) { return g.name === 'DDD Warsaw'; });
pm.test('ProposalAccepted event created group DDD Warsaw', function () { pm.expect(group).to.not.be.undefined; });

item.name: Payments
item.description: Member token. 1. Buy a subscription (payerLogin 'ada' must own a group, see Administration) → 2. Verify SubscriptionPurchased (any member: paymentValidUntil stamped on ada's group) → 3. List (admin). Pay a meeting fee once a meeting exists.

item.name: Verify SubscriptionPurchased event → group marked paid
item.description: Any member token, ~10s after Buy subscription — re-send until green. Proves SubscriptionPurchasedIntegrationEvent travelled Payments → Meetings and ExtendGroupPaymentOnSubscriptionHandler stamped paymentValidUntil. Only works when the payer owns a group: the default flow uses payerLogin 'ada' together with the group proposed by 'ada'.

exec: pm.test('payer ada owns a group', function () { pm.expect(group).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test('SubscriptionPurchased event marked the group paid', function () { pm.expect(group && group.paymentValidUntil).to.not.be.null; });

item.name: Meetings
item.description: Member token for view/join/comment; organizer token for create. List groups first (captures groupId), then create a meeting, join, comment, and list attendees. Body meetingId/groupId MUST match the route value.
